section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department correspondence and records from June 1947 to December 1949 concerning the Japanese iron and steel industry under Allied occupation. Major topics include Far Eastern Commission policy decisions and SCAP directives extending the temporary retention of electric steel furnaces to alleviate postwar coal shortages while addressing Allied reparations concerns. The records also document inquiries regarding steel and pig iron allocations for textile machinery, missions and commercial proposals to survey and export Japanese iron and steel scrap to the United States and Canada, and technical reports on fuel economy and record postwar steel and pig iron production.

subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Secretary General Nelson T. Johnson transmits certified policy decision FEC-239/7 extending Japanese electric steel furnace retention up to an additional 300,000 metric tons annual capacity until June 30, 1948, due to continued coal shortages. The enclosure includes certified minutes of the 67th FEC meeting detailing statements by Chinese delegate Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo regarding capacity estimates and balanced reparations removals, as well as the French delegation's abstention.
subfiles.title: Extension of Far Eastern Commission Policy on Temporary Retention of Electric Steel Furnaces (FEC-239/7)
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State

subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary J. H. Hilldring submits a draft directive implementing Far Eastern Commission policy FEC-239/7 to extend electric steel furnace retention in Japan through June 30, 1948. He requests transmittal via the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General MacArthur, accompanied by Chinese Representative Dr. Koo's statement for information. Enclosures include the draft directive to SCAP and excerpted minutes of the 67th FEC meeting.
subfiles.title: Draft Directive regarding Extension of Far Eastern Commission Policy on Temporary Retention of Electric Steel Furnaces

subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP letter and technical report by Caleb Davies, Jr. on fuel utilization and coalite coke in Japanese steelmaking.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan (signed by E. G. Seidensticker, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 786 forwards SCAP correspondence with Dr. P. S. Lokanathan of ECAFE and a detailed technical report by consultant Caleb Davies, Jr. on recent fuel economy practices in the Japanese iron and steel industry. Davies outlines the adoption of automatic combustion controls, powdered coal, and especially the Wanishi Works' 'coalite' process of blending low-temperature carbonized non-coking coal with inferior coking coal to produce strong metallurgical blast furnace coke without imported coal. The report notes successful applications at Amagasaki Steel and Wanishi, highlighting equipment suppliers and operational practices for low-grade coal and iron ore beneficiation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 786: Developments in Fuel Utilization for Manufacturing Iron and Steel
